    Maps factoring through sums of copies of a fixed module #

    Lemma 2.6. Fix a module P. On modules without a direct summand isomorphic to P, the maps factoring through a direct sum P^(I) of copies of P form an ideal J, and every composite of ℓ + 1 maps of J vanishes as soon as every product of ℓ nonunits of End_A(P) vanishes.

    The manuscript assumes that P is finite-dimensional and indecomposable and that (rad End_A(P))^ℓ = 0. Then End_A(P) is local (Fitting's lemma), so its nonunits are exactly its radical, and the hypothesis used here, NonunitProductsVanish P ℓ, is equivalent to the manuscript's; see nonunitProductsVanish_of_isLocalRing. The proof below does not need the finite generation of P: it tracks images of single vectors instead of matrix columns.
